page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-48xCPU-384GB is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by the AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Virtualized via KVM, the system allocates 48 shared vCPUs mapped across 48 physical cores with 1 thread per core. The instance is provisioned with 384.0 GB of system memory, establishing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions, but it lacks AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets. The server includes no integrated GPUs and comes with no bundled local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote network storage configurations for persistent disk needs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong aggregate parallel compute and decompression performance alongside middle-tier per-core metrics. In multi-threaded workloads, the instance achieves top-quartile results with a PassMark CPU score of 56,420.04 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 341.35 GB/sec. Conversely, the 2.0 GHz clock speed results in lower single-threaded metrics, illustrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 768.79. Memory bandwidth tests record 127.36 GB/sec for uncached read-only streams and 62.7 GB/sec for write streams. In web and cache service tests, it maintains a static web serving throughput of 23.13 GB/sec and handles 55.56 million Redis SET operations per second.

Given its high memory density and 48 physical execution cores, this instance delivers efficient capacity scaling for parallelized enterprise applications. However, organizations should consider the performance tradeoffs associated with shared CPU resource allocation and lower single-core frequency. It is best suited for memory-intensive applications, in-memory databases, caching layers, distributed ETL batch processing, and horizontally scalable backend services that can exploit large core counts and high RAM without requiring local NVMe disks or hardware accelerators.

Built on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 384.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration includes no local storage or GPUs. Benchmark testing highlights strong multi-threaded capabilities, scoring 56,420.04 in PassMark CPU and 341.35 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, though single-core throughput remains modest. Memory operations achieve 127.36 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, while Redis SET throughput reaches 55.56 million operations per second. The instance provides resource density suited for large memory footprints, making it appropriate for in-memory databases, distributed caching, ETL pipelines, and scalable enterprise web services.
